title: Word cards under a fixed page margin
method:
A clerk fills the width of a line with word cards of different widths. One EVA-basic glyph or one separator takes one width unit. From certain words on the 192 public practice-training folios, count word cards regardless of their positions, in separate drawers by line kind. Complete, certain training lines supply the capacity distribution for each kind. Use the public line-kind and paragraph-opening layout of the book. Sample one margin capacity for each line. At every slot, draw from the cards that fit in the remaining width, paying the separator when needed. Stop when no card fits. The fitted margin rule has no fixed token cutoff for short words. The matched stop control uses the same sampled widths. After a fitting first word it ends on the first unconstrained card that would cross the margin. Another control shuffles the entire word inventory inside each primary line. The manuscript-wide public four-word copy guard applies. Seed 408 is the fixed primary specimen, and seed 409 checks sensitivity. The primary produces 5,225 lines and 40,065 tokens.

Public practice: short words are 425/652 (65.18%) at line ends and 1,348/4,421 (30.49%) in interiors, ratio 2.137824 and within-line shuffle p=0.0025. The manuscript's ratio is 1.157454. The paired first-nonfitting-stop and within-line-shuffle controls give ratios 0.986280 and 1.011232 with p=0.175 and p=0.405. Sensitivity seed 409 gives ratio 2.093918 and p=0.0025. The procedure clears the threshold with a stronger short-word surplus than the manuscript.
